original_metadata.title: A complex Laurent-polynomial mutation z1 to z1 divided by a nonzero Laurent polynomial in the other variables, preserving Laurentness and with the origin interior to the initial Newton polytope, places the two face-fan toric varieties in one flat projective family over P1
original_metadata.author: Nathan Owen Ilten
original_metadata.source_title: Mutations of Laurent Polynomials and Flat Families with Toric Fibers
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof turns an arbitrary-dimensional Laurent mutation into explicit Newton-slice polyhedra and an integral admissible Minkowski pair for a torus-equivariant deformation. It then identifies the mutated cone through the two tailcone inclusions and checks the degree-zero projectivization needed for a flat projective family over P1. The full construction is beyond a toric fan definition check; the previously established p-divisor family theorem is used only after these new coefficients are supplied.

proof_review.note: Full Theorem1.3 for the special Example1.2 mutation is selected. Read all Example1.2/Definition1.4 assumptions, complete Section2 affine torus-variety/p-divisor construction and its admissibility/degree-zero projectivization conditions, and every Section3 Newton-slice, Minkowski, mutated-cone and two-tailcone-inclusion argument. The prior Ilten-Vollmert[5] construction supplies the flat family; the author gives the actual coefficient polyhedra and infinity fiber in Theorem2.1 and checks both admissible pairs through the integral Delta(g). The omitted second tailcone inclusion is explicitly the same reverse argument, ancillary to the displayed full forward construction, not a missing new family core. The theorem is not for arbitrary birational volume-preserving mutations and does not assert every fiber is toric, a smooth total space or a Q-Gorenstein smoothing. Surface examples/general deformation criterion are context and not additional counts.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1.3 over C. f is a Laurent polynomial in n variables with Newton polytope Delta(f) containing0 in its interior. g is a nonzero Laurent polynomial in z2,...,zn; phi changes z1 to z1/g and fixes the other variables. The required Laurentness means every positive-z1 coefficient f_i is divisible by g^i in the Laurent ring, as in Example1.2. Then a flat projective family X->P1 has fiber0=TV(Delta(f)) and fiber infinity=TV(Delta(phi(f))), where TV uses the face fan. No general mutation, every-fiber toricity or Q-Gorenstein/smoothness assertion is selected.

The named prior Ilten-Vollmert construction remains a prerequisite, with the author actual coefficients, admissibility and infinity fibre supplied.
